findings.message: The ban on looking up the story's own estimate is stated three times (intro, first bullet of 'What not to read', and the ID-search bullet).
findings.detail: "the other card exists but you must not look for it"; "Never look for an estimate of the story you are estimating or of its tasks, wherever it is"; "Do not search the repo for the story's ID or its tasks' IDs." The last is a concrete means of the second, so it adds a little, but the intro line is a pure restatement. Consolidated wording: keep the 'What not to read' rule ("Never look for an estimate of this story or its tasks, and do not search the repo for their IDs") and shorten the intro to "you estimate alone and blind".

findings.message: The second bullet of "What to read" (the epic's source document) folds three reading rules into one paragraph.
findings.detail:
Opens with "The epic's **source document**. The story's `**Épica:**` line… gives the prefix". Proposed checklist:
- [ ] Take the epic prefix (H1, PB…) from the story's `**Épica:**` line or its parent issue's title.
- [ ] Find the source document and where each part lives in the table in `docs/instructions/workflow.md` §3.
- [ ] Read through that table, never by a section number you remember.
- [ ] Cover users, expectations, scope, assumptions, constraints, open questions and glossary.

findings.message: The ban on design and implementation questions is stated three times (What to read, Format, Guidelines).
findings.detail: Quotes: "they pull you towards design questions, which belong to the OpenSpec change, not to the story" (What to read); "phrased as a concrete question or situation, not as a solution" (Format); "Do not ask about implementation (types, formats, protocols, internal contracts): that is the spec's job" (Guidelines). Consolidated wording: keep the single rule in Guidelines ("Do not ask about implementation or propose solutions: design belongs to the OpenSpec change") and shorten the other two to the reading restriction only.

findings.message: "Use it sparingly" for the `spec` tag gives no limit or criterion for when it is allowed.
findings.detail: "`spec`: a design question for the OpenSpec change. Use it sparingly." Readings: at most one of the 3 out-of-criteria notes, or only when no other tag fits. The guidelines already ban implementation questions, so behaviour barely changes. Rewrite: "`spec`: a design question for the OpenSpec change. At most one per review, and only when none of the other tags fits."

findings.message: The quota guidance restates the same point three ways in two sentences (about 15 words could be saved).
findings.detail: "Return fewer if you find fewer: there is no quota. Five solid ones beat eight padded ones." Tightened: "Return fewer if you find fewer; there is no quota."

findings.message: Step 2 ("Gather the evidence") packs four discrete directives into one paragraph.
findings.detail:
Opening: "From this conversation, pick only what backs the user's words..."
- [ ] Pick only what backs the user's words and that the subagent could not know: links, `file:line`, PR and job IDs, commits, short log excerpts (a few lines, not whole logs), trace IDs.
- [ ] Add a line `De dónde sale: MOO-n` with the Linear issue or PR the session is working on, if the need came out of it.
- [ ] Copy the evidence; do not summarise, classify or give your opinion (the subagent suggests the type, the user decides it).
- [ ] If the conversation holds nothing relevant, write `Sin evidencia`.

findings.message: The Input paragraph encodes three discrete directives about not interrupting the user.
findings.detail:
Opening: "Input: `$ARGUMENTS` = the user's words. The user typing `/capture` is the request..."
- [ ] Treat the user typing `/capture` as the request itself.
- [ ] Do not ask the user for confirmation.
- [ ] Do not ask questions to improve the capture (any question is the interruption this skill exists to avoid).

findings.message: "short log excerpts (a few lines, not whole logs)" gives no line count for how much log to copy into the evidence.
findings.detail: "short log excerpts (a few lines, not whole logs)". Readings range from 3 to 30 lines, which changes how much text reaches the capture. Rewrite: "log excerpts of at most 10 lines around the error." Only the author can fix the exact number.

findings.message: The «Title» paragraph encodes four title rules in narrative form.
findings.detail:
Opens with «Short, in Spanish, naming the need or what was seen, not an action…». Proposed checklist:
- [ ] Write the title short.
- [ ] Write the title in Spanish.
- [ ] Name the need or what was seen, not an action (an action presumes a type, which is decided when classifying).
- [ ] Never start the title with a verb in the infinitive, even when the user's own words do (e.g. «Nivel de audio en grande en el panel», not «Ver el nivel de audio en grande»).
- [ ] Keep the user's vocabulary otherwise.

findings.message: The «Writing it» opening paragraph encodes about four tool and scope restrictions in prose.
findings.detail:
Opens with «Your only tools here are `Read`…». Proposed checklist:
- [ ] Use only `Read` (for `docs/instructions/linear.md`) and the Linear MCP's `save_issue`.
- [ ] Do not edit files.
- [ ] Do not run commands.
- [ ] Do not call any other Linear tool.
- [ ] If `save_issue` is not loaded, load it with `ToolSearch` (`select:mcp__linear__save_issue`).

findings.message: The closing failure paragraph packs two directives (never retry in another state, report the failure).
findings.detail:
Opens with «If the call fails, do not retry in another state…». Proposed checklist:
- [ ] If `save_issue` fails, do not retry in another state (e.g. Backlog): a capture outside Triage gets lost among refined work.
- [ ] Report the failure (`status: failed` with the error).

findings.message: The rule that the capturer must not decide classification fields is stated twice (intro and 'Nothing else' list).
findings.detail: "You do not decide anything that classifying decides (type, epic, priority, duplicates): you only suggest." and "Nothing else: no `labels`, `priority`, `parentId`, `estimate` or `assignee`. They are set when classifying...". Consolidate: keep the intro statement and have the Writing section only list the permitted fields, noting that everything else is left for classifying.

findings.message: The 'title is not an action / no infinitive verb' rule is restated within the Title paragraph (3 phrasings).
findings.detail: "not an action", "An action already presumes a type...", "So the title never starts with a verb in the infinitive". Consolidate: "The title names the need or what was seen, never an action (no leading infinitive verb, since an action presumes a type); e.g. 'Nivel de audio en grande en el panel'."

findings.message: The title directive asks for a "short" title without a length limit.
findings.detail: Quote: "**Title.** Short, in Spanish, naming the need or what was seen". Readings: 5 words, 10 words, or one line; the result barely changes behaviour. Proposed rewrite: "Title: at most 10 words, in Spanish, naming the need or what was seen."

findings.message: The goal "write it down faithfully and fast" gives no acceptance criterion for "fast".
findings.detail: Quote: "Your job is to write it down faithfully and fast". Readings: minimal tool calls, or no extra reasoning; the rest of the document (one save_issue call, no other tools) already narrows it. Proposed rewrite: "Create the capture with a single save_issue call and no other Linear calls."

findings.message: Step 4 ("What comes out of it") encodes three discrete directives in one paragraph.
findings.detail:
Opening: "Propose the stories, bugs or chores the verdict opens..."
- [ ] Propose the stories, bugs or chores the verdict opens, and any story the spike blocked that can now be refined.
- [ ] For each one the user keeps, give them a ready-made `/capture <texto>` line to run (captures are the user's to launch; they go through the usual classification).
- [ ] Write them in the spike document too.

findings.message: The closing paragraph of step 2 hides two ordered directives about the verdict and its approval.
findings.detail:
Opening: "Then draft the **verdict**: the decision the answers lead to..."
- [ ] Draft the verdict: the decision the answers lead to, in one or two sentences, checked against the deliverable the spike promised.
- [ ] Let the user correct or rewrite it.
- [ ] Do not move on until the user approves it (every later step writes it down).

findings.message: That the user decides and approves the verdict before anything is written is stated twice (intro and step 2).
findings.detail: "**The decision is the user's**: you draft, they decide." and "The user corrects or rewrites it. Do not move on until they approve it, because every later step writes it down." Consolidate: keep step 2's gating rule and trim the intro to "you draft the verdict; the user approves it (step 2)."

findings.message: The directive on uncommitted changes says to ask whether they belong to the experiment but not what to do for each answer.
findings.detail: "If there are uncommitted changes, ask whether they belong to the experiment before going on." If the user says yes, the skill does not say whether to commit them first; if no, it does not say whether to stash, leave, or stop. Suggested rewrite: "If there are uncommitted changes, ask whether they belong to the experiment: if yes, commit them with `Refs MOO-n` before continuing; if no, stop and ask the user to set them aside."

findings.message: Step 4 ("Timebox") encodes three discrete directives in one paragraph.
findings.detail:
Opening: "Ask the user for it: **½, 1 or 2 days** of dedicated work..."
- [ ] Ask the user for the timebox: ½, 1 or 2 days of dedicated work.
- [ ] Do not propose a value (the user sets it; a number from you would anchor them).
- [ ] If the work is more than 2 days, propose splitting the spike, as a 13 splits a story.

findings.message: Step 6 ("Non-goals") encodes three discrete directives in prose.
findings.detail:
Opening: "What the spike will not answer or build. Production code is always one of them..."
- [ ] List 2-4 non-goals: what the spike will not answer or build.
- [ ] Always include production code as a non-goal (anything that should stay goes through the normal lane afterwards, as a capture or a story).
- [ ] Take the remaining non-goals from the source document and from sibling stories and spikes.

findings.message: Step 9 ("Human gate") hides four discrete directives in one paragraph.
findings.detail:
Opening: "Build the description from `assets/spike.md` and show it..."
- [ ] Build the description from `assets/spike.md` and show it to the user.
- [ ] For a new spike, also show the title, labels, priority and relations.
- [ ] For an existing issue, put its current description under **Contexto** unchanged, except a capture's «Clasificación sugerida», which the classification already settled.
- [ ] Write nothing to Linear until the user approves.

findings.message: The third bullet of step 1 ("The epic's source document.") packs four discrete directives into one dense paragraph.
findings.detail:
Opens with "The epic's source document. The prefix of the epic's title (`H1`, `S2`, `PB`…) tells you which one it is…". Proposed checklist:
- [ ] Identify the source document from the prefix of the epic's title (H1, S2, PB…).
- [ ] Read the parts you need through the table in `docs/instructions/workflow.md` §3, never by a section number you remember.
- [ ] If the epic is not in the table (e.g. EN), stop and say so.
- [ ] Treat the source document as the source of truth: mark anything it does not back as *(asumido)* instead of presenting it as fact.

findings.message: The rule that nothing is written to Linear before the user validates is stated twice (intro and step 3).
findings.detail: Quotes: "the user validates every story before anything is written to Linear" (intro) and "Nothing goes to Linear without explicit approval" (step 3). Consolidated wording: keep the rule only in step 3 (Human gate) and drop the clause from the Input paragraph.

findings.message: "Read the parts you need" of the source document does not say which parts count as needed.
findings.detail: "Read the parts you need through that table... the epic's story or stories..., its expectations, scope, users, open questions and glossary." The list that follows mostly resolves it, so the ambiguity rarely changes behaviour. Tighten: "Read the epic's stories, expectations, scope, users, open questions and glossary through that table."

findings.message: Step 1 (Precondition) encodes about seven branching directives for Spike and unrefined stories in a single paragraph.
findings.detail:
Opens: "Read the story with `get_issue`. If it carries the **`Spike`** label, stop...". Proposed checklist:
- [ ] Read the story with `get_issue`.
- [ ] If it carries the `Spike` label, stop: its timebox replaces the estimate (`linear.md` §4).
- [ ] Spike with no timebox yet: point to `/create-spike <id>`.
- [ ] Spike with a timebox: say it is ready to start.
- [ ] For a Spike, ask for no card and launch no estimator.
- [ ] Otherwise, require the story to be refined (GWT criteria, non-goals and a DoD).
- [ ] If it is not refined, stop and point to `/refine-story` (an estimate of an unrefined story measures uncertainty, not effort).

findings.message: Step 4 (Reveal) packs about five directives on showing the cards and who decides into prose and a short bullet pair.
findings.detail:
Opens: "Show both cards side by side, each with its reason." ... "The user decides the final number...". Proposed checklist:
- [ ] Show both cards side by side, each with its reason.
- [ ] If the cards match, use that as the estimate.
- [ ] If they differ, summarise which assumption each one is making.
- [ ] Let the user decide the final number.
- [ ] Do not average the cards and do not break the tie yourself (the user is accountable for the estimate).

findings.message: Step 5 (Poke-holes) packs five discrete directives about what to hand the subagent into one dense paragraph.
findings.detail:
Opens: "Once the user has validated the translation, launch the **`poke-holes`** subagent and give it only the story ID...". Proposed checklist:
- [ ] Launch the `poke-holes` subagent only after the user has validated the GWT translation.
- [ ] Give it only the story ID, the Como/quiero/para, the non-goals and the happy path.
- [ ] Pass the happy path in the user's own words: their step 2 answer plus any correction or clarification written while validating the translation in step 4.
- [ ] Never pass your GWT translation (it carries your blind spots and *(asumido)* fills).
- [ ] Do not pass this conversation.

findings.message: Step 3 (Quick INVEST) encodes about six directives, including a stop condition and three prohibitions, in a single paragraph.
findings.detail:
Opens: "With the Como/quiero/para, the non-goals and the user's description, give one line per criterion...". Proposed checklist:
- [ ] Give one line per INVEST criterion (Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable) with ✅/⚠️/❌ and a reason.
- [ ] If two or more criteria fail, propose how to split the story into 2-3 stories, each with its own observable behaviour, citing evidence from the user's description, and stop there.
- [ ] When stopping on a failed INVEST, do not translate the description.
- [ ] When stopping on a failed INVEST, do not launch poke-holes.
- [ ] When stopping on a failed INVEST, do not write anything to Linear.
- [ ] If it passes, show the result briefly and carry on; the full check returns in step 9.

findings.message: Step 5 interleaves its input constraints with rationale, so the "never pass the GWT translation" rule sits mid-paragraph between two explanations.
findings.detail: Spans: "Never your GWT translation. Do not pass this conversation." and "The value of the subagent is that it has not seen what was already decided...". Proposal: put the subagent's inputs and prohibitions first as a short list (pass: story ID, Como/quiero/para, non-goals, happy path in the user's words incl. step-4 corrections; never pass: the GWT translation, this conversation), then the rationale in one trailing paragraph, then the return format.

findings.message: Step 3 buries the pass branch ("If it passes, show it briefly and carry on") after a long failure branch with its rationale.
findings.detail: Spans: "If it fails **two or more**, the story is not ready..." and "If it passes, show it briefly and carry on; the full check comes back in step 9." Proposal: split into the INVEST line-per-criterion instruction, then two short bullets ("Fails two or more: ..." / "Passes: ..."), moving the "why it goes here" explanation to the end.

findings.message: The description hides that the skill writes to Linear (updates the story and creates task sub-issues) and that Spike-labelled issues are refused.
findings.detail: Current description: "Refine a Mood Table user story that is in Backlog in Linear. ... adds the DoD by type, technical context and the proposed tasks." Body evidence: step 12 calls `save_issue` to update the story and create each approved task as a sub-issue; step 1 stops for issues labelled `Spike`. It does cue the moment (story in Backlog, second step of the flow), so the mismatch is minor. Suggested: "Refine a Mood Table user story in Backlog in Linear (not a Spike): the user writes the happy path, the AI translates it to GIVEN/WHEN/THEN, the poke-holes subagent finds gaps and the user keeps 3-5; checks INVEST (stops to propose a split if it fails), adds the DoD by type and technical context, and after approval saves the story and creates its task sub-issues. Use after /create-story and before /estimate-story."

findings.message: "If it fails two or more" INVEST criteria does not say whether a ⚠️ counts as a failure or only ❌ does.
findings.detail: Steps 3 and 9 grade each criterion ✅/⚠️/❌, then say "If it fails **two or more**, the story is not ready". Reading A: only ❌ counts; reading B: ⚠️ and ❌ both count. They lead to different actions (split vs. continue). Rewrite: "If two or more criteria are ❌, the story is not ready: propose how to split it..." (or state that ⚠️ counts too).

findings.message: "show it briefly and carry on" leaves the length of the passing INVEST summary unspecified.
findings.detail: "If it passes, show it briefly and carry on; the full check comes back in step 9." Candidate readings: the six one-line results, or just a one-line verdict. Rewrite: "If it passes, show the six one-line results and carry on."

findings.message: Step 5 explains twice why the subagent must not see the GWT translation; about two sentences could be cut.
findings.detail: Quote: "The value of the subagent is that it has not seen what was already decided, so it does not share the author's blind spots. Your translation is already an interpretation, with its (asumido) gaps filled in your way; passing it would hand the subagent your blind spots too." Tightened wording: "Never pass your GWT translation: it carries your (asumido) gaps and would hand the subagent your blind spots."

findings.message: The «Commands» setup paragraph encodes about three environment prerequisites in prose.
findings.detail:
Opens with «Node 24 (`.nvmrc`; `nvm use`) and pnpm from `packageManager`…». Proposed checklist:
- [ ] Use Node 24 (`.nvmrc`; run `nvm use`).
- [ ] Enable pnpm from `packageManager` via `corepack enable`.
- [ ] Do not rely on `corepack pnpm` alone: scripts call `pnpm` inside (`typecheck`, the E2E web server) and fail without it.

findings.message: The opening «Read before working…» paragraph encodes about four reading directives with a conditional exception.
findings.detail:
Opens with «Read before working on product or design questions…». Proposed checklist:
- [ ] Before product or design questions, read `docs/PRD.md` (source of truth for what and why; glossary in §8).
- [ ] Before product or design questions, read `readme.md` (architecture, data model, stories, tickets).
- [ ] Before product or design questions, read `docs/idea-mood-table.md` §10 (decisions D1-D39 with their rationale).
- [ ] For the PR Babysitter epic (development tooling, not product), read `docs/pr-babysitter.md` instead of the PRD.

findings.message: The 'grey areas or risks' trigger for stopping gives no test for when a decision qualifies.
findings.detail: "When a decision has grey areas or risks, stop and say so, with reasoning and alternatives." Two agents could disagree on whether a decision is grey, so the stop rule fires inconsistently. Suggested rewrite: "Stop and say so when a decision is not covered by the PRD, README or D# decisions, or when it is hard to reverse (schema, public API, hardware wiring); give reasoning and at least two alternatives."

findings.message: 'Complete before extensive' gives no criterion for when a flow counts as complete.
findings.detail: "Complete before extensive: one closed, excellent flow beats broad coverage." It does not say what makes a flow closed or excellent, so an agent cannot decide when to stop polishing one flow and start another. Suggested rewrite: "Finish one flow end to end (its acceptance criteria met, tests green, DoD checked) before starting another."

findings.message: The Regla/Formato paragraphs in §5 (`prompts.md`) encode four discrete directives in two run-on lines.
findings.detail:
Opens: "**Regla:** al cerrar una sección del README o un hito del arnés, se registra en `prompts.md`. **Formato:** como mucho **3 prompts** por sección...". Proposed checklist:
- [ ] Al cerrar una sección del README o un hito del arnés, registrarlo en `prompts.md`.
- [ ] Incluir como mucho 3 prompts por sección, solo los que aporten.
- [ ] Copiar los prompts literalmente, sin corregir ni recortar.
- [ ] Añadir una línea en cursiva con el contexto y el resultado de cada prompt.

findings.message: That `readme.md` and `prompts.md` are mandatory is stated twice in §3 (the template line and the closing bullet of the delivery mechanics).
findings.detail: "**Plantilla oficial:** un `readme.md` con 8 secciones + `prompts.md`." and "`readme.md` y `prompts.md`, obligatorios siempre." Consolidated wording: keep only the template line and add "(ambos obligatorios en cada entrega)".

findings.message: The extension request says to ask the TA "con antelación" without giving a lead time.
findings.detail: Quote: "Prórroga posible hasta el 25-nov, pidiéndola al TA con antelación". Readings: days before the delivery date, or before the deadline passes. Only the author or LIDR can fix the number. Proposed rewrite: "pidiéndola al TA al menos N días antes de la fecha de entrega (N a confirmar con el TA)".

findings.message: The tip "iterar el PRD hasta que lo cubra todo" has no acceptance criterion for "todo".
findings.detail: Quote: "iterar el PRD hasta que lo cubra todo". Readings: every story and expectation of the idea, every evaluation axis, or every section of the official template. Proposed rewrite: "iterar el PRD hasta que cada historia tenga expectativas, alcance y glosario, y cada decisión dé juego en los tres ejes (§2)".

findings.message: The single paragraph of §6 (Tareas) encodes five discrete task-writing rules in prose.
findings.detail:
Opens with "**Una tarea = una PR** (ver `workflow.md` §2). Título en imperativo…". Proposed checklist:
- [ ] Una tarea = una PR.
- [ ] Escribe el título en imperativo.
- [ ] Ponle una sola etiqueta de área.
- [ ] Describe en una o dos líneas qué se integra.
- [ ] No copies el detalle paso a paso: vive en su sección del `tasks.md` del OpenSpec change (un paso = un commit) y la tarea lo enlaza.
- [ ] Si es una *chore* sin change (`workflow.md` §6), pon ese plan en la descripción de la tarea.
- [ ] Un *spike* no lleva tareas: es una sola PR (`workflow.md` §7).

findings.message: The "Hook `validate-ac`" bullet in §8 packs about five format requirements for acceptance criteria into one paragraph.
findings.detail:
Opens with "antes de guardar, revisa el formato de la sección `## Criterios de aceptación`…". Proposed checklist of what the hook enforces:
- [ ] Cada escenario lleva Given, When y Then, en ese orden.
- [ ] Cada escenario tiene un solo When (sin And ni But que lo continúe).
- [ ] Sin huecos de la plantilla.
- [ ] Los esquemas del escenario usan como parámetros columnas de su tabla de ejemplos.
- [ ] Sin la sección `## Criterios de aceptación`, o con la marca de pendiente de `/create-story`, no se valida nada (solo se mira la forma, no el contenido).

findings.message: The GitHub-driven state transitions (draft PR, open PR, merged PR) are listed in the §2 state table and again in the §7 automations bullet (two statements).
findings.detail: §2: "In Progress | Implementándose (PR en borrador) | GitHub (automático)", "In Review | PR abierta...", "Done | PR integrada". §7: "Automatizaciones: PR en borrador → `In Progress` · PR abierta → `In Review` · revisión pedida → `In Review` · PR integrada → `Done`." Only 'revisión pedida → In Review' is new. Consolidated wording: in §7 keep just "Automatizaciones: las de la tabla de estados (§2), más revisión pedida → `In Review`."

findings.message: The «Puertas de la PR» bullet in §7 documents GitHub ruleset and Codex settings, which are PR-merge configuration rather than Linear conventions.
findings.detail: Span: «Puertas de la PR, que configura el usuario: en el ruleset «ramas de integración»… en los ajustes de Codex (Code review)…» (required checks, `required_review_thread_resolution`, automatic Codex review). It serves the PR gates, a GitHub/CI concern; the Linear link only needs the branch/ID/PR-keyword rules around it. Resolution: relocate it to `docs/instructions/workflow.md` §4 (which already lists the gates) and leave a one-line cross-reference here.

findings.message: The directive to review the permission list when Linear publishes new tools names no trigger, owner or check.
findings.detail: Quote: "Las herramientas nuevas que publique Linear no quedan cubiertas: caen en el modo de permisos por defecto. Hay que revisar la lista si aparece alguna." Readings: review on every Linear MCP update, or only when someone notices a new tool; and which list (the allow/ask/deny entries in .claude/settings.json). Proposed rewrite: "Cuando `mcp__linear__*` exponga una herramienta que no esté en `allow` ni en `deny` de `.claude/settings.json`, el mantenedor la añade a `allow`, `ask` o `deny` en la misma PR que la use."

findings.message: That a panel ignores a message type it does not know is stated three times (type 5 notes, type 7 notes, and the closing section).
findings.detail: "Un panel que no conoce el tipo `5` lo ignora."; "Un panel que no conoce el tipo `7` lo ignora."; "Lo ignora, también si es de un tipo que todavía no conoce." The closing section already covers every type, present and future. Consolidated wording: drop the two per-type sentences and keep only the closing rule, "Un panel ignora cualquier mensaje que no entiende, también el de un tipo que todavía no conoce."

findings.message: The opening blockquote mixes the document's key maintenance rule with a long change-by-change provenance list, so the rule is easy to skim past.
findings.detail: The blockquote starting «Fuente de verdad del formato…» ends its first paragraph with «Si cambia el formato, cambian este documento y ese código en la misma PR.» and then runs straight into «Origen: change `virtual-strip-breathing`…» listing eight changes and tickets. Proposal: keep the source-of-truth statement and the same-PR rule in the blockquote, and move the origin list to a short «## Origen» section at the end of the document (or a bulleted list there), preserving all content.

findings.message: El bullet de §4 paso 4 «Antes de integrar, el agente comprueba que Codex ha revisado el último push» esconde cuatro reglas condicionales en un solo párrafo.
findings.detail:
Apertura: "Antes de integrar, el agente comprueba que Codex ha revisado el último push..."
- [ ] Antes de integrar, comprobar que Codex ha revisado el último push.
- [ ] Sin hallazgos, Codex no deja una revisión de GitHub sino un comentario de `chatgpt-codex-connector` con el commit revisado (`commit_sha` en su bloque `codex-review-state`): leer ese comentario.
- [ ] El `commit_sha` tiene que coincidir con el último commit de la PR.
- [ ] Si no coincide o no hay comentario (p. ej., límite de uso agotado, que Codex no avisa), pedir la revisión con un comentario `@codex review` o decírselo al usuario.

findings.message: El bullet «Cada hallazgo de Codex o de SonarQube» de §4 paso 4 codifica cinco reglas de tratamiento de hallazgos en prosa.
findings.detail:
Apertura: "**Cada hallazgo de Codex o de SonarQube**, el agente lo **verifica** contra el código..."
- [ ] Verificar cada hallazgo de Codex o de SonarQube contra el código; no darlo por bueno.
- [ ] Si es real, arreglarlo con un commit y contestar en el hilo con el commit.
- [ ] Si no aplica, contestar en el hilo por qué.
- [ ] Resolver el hilo después de contestar.
- [ ] En SonarQube, marcar lo que no aplica como aceptado por el usuario, con el motivo.

findings.message: El párrafo «Documentos fuente» de §3 contiene cuatro directivas sobre cómo citar y mantener la tabla de secciones.
findings.detail:
Apertura: "**Documentos fuente.** El PRD y `docs/pr-babysitter.md` son los **documentos fuente**..."
- [ ] Citar un documento fuente por su ID y el número de sección (`PRD §5.4`, `PB §5.3`), y sus elementos por su propio ID (E3, BA2).
- [ ] Tratar la tabla de partes como el único sitio que dice en qué sección está cada parte.
- [ ] Quien necesite una parte (p. ej. las skills de historias) la lee en esa tabla y no lleva los números escritos.
- [ ] Si un documento se renumera, actualizar la tabla en el mismo commit.

findings.message: El paso 3 «Cerrar» de §7 reúne seis directivas de cierre de un spike en un párrafo.
findings.detail:
Apertura: "**Cerrar** (`/close-spike`). El usuario aprueba el veredicto y anota el tiempo dedicado..."
- [ ] El usuario aprueba el veredicto.
- [ ] Anotar el tiempo dedicado junto al *timebox* (solo se anota; agotarlo no obliga a nada).
- [ ] Apuntar lo que sale del spike como capturas.
- [ ] Borrar el prototipo de la rama.
- [ ] Enlazar el prototipo desde la PR por su commit (con *squash* los commits de la rama no llegan a `main`, pero GitHub conserva los de cada PR).
- [ ] Dejar como diff solo el veredicto y pasar la PR a lista para revisar.

findings.message: The rule "one task = one PR, one step = one commit" is restated in the chain table, in §2 and again in §5 (3 times).
findings.detail: §1: "una tarea = una PR" / "cada paso = un commit"; §2 title "Granularidad: tarea → PR, paso → commit" and its table; §5: "Tarea → PR, paso → commit: no mezclar dos tareas en una PR ni dos pasos en un commit." Keep §2 as the single statement and reduce §5 to a pointer: "Tarea → PR, paso → commit (§2); un spike es una PR con commits libres (§7)."

findings.message: "Write each datum in one place and link elsewhere" appears in §3 and again in §5 ("No duplicar").
findings.detail: §3: "Cada dato se escribe en **un solo sitio**; en los demás, se enlaza." and §5: "**No duplicar:** si algo ya está en otro sitio de la tabla del §3, enlázalo." Consolidate by keeping §3 and dropping the §5 bullet, or making it a bare cross-reference.

findings.message: Step 4 «PR» in §4 packs the gates, the per-finding handling and the pre-merge Codex check into one long list item, so the last-push check is easy to miss.
findings.detail: Step 4 («PR (una por tarea), contra `main`…») runs from the gate list through «Cada hallazgo de Codex o de SonarQube…» to «Antes de integrar, el agente comprueba que Codex ha revisado el último push…». The last bullet is a distinct pre-merge procedure (match `commit_sha` in `codex-review-state` with the last commit, otherwise ask with `@codex review`). Proposal: split step 4 into named sub-steps (4a Abrir y puertas, 4b Tratar los hallazgos, 4c Antes de integrar) or promote the Codex check to its own step between 4 and 5, so the pre-merge condition has its own heading.
